bank: Get a job: questions for each job (round 1)
note: learn pages, quiz and challenge from the first round; harder: five optional questions after a job is finished, which unlock the job trophy

learn.text: Architects draw plans. A plan is a picture from above that shows where every wall, door and window goes.
Architects measure first. They check how big a room is and where the sun comes in, before they draw anything.

choices: To know how big things are
quiz.a: To know how big things are

choices: Where the walls and windows go
quiz.a: Where the walls and windows go

challenge.scene: A family wants a window in the kitchen, but the wall is short.
challenge.question: Ask someone who builds houses: what are some ways to solve this?
choices: Move the window up a little

task.prompt: First pass: where should the bed go in the plan, so it does not block the door?
choices: Next to the wall, away from the door
In the middle of the doorway
task.a: Next to the wall, away from the door

harder.q: A client wants a bigger kitchen, but the house has only one small space for it. What should an architect do first?
choices: Measure the space and draw two plan ideas
Tell the client to find a different house
Knock down the walls without a plan
harder.a: Measure the space and draw two plan ideas
harder.why: Measuring and drawing ideas show what will fit before any building starts.

harder.q: Why do architects draw a plan from above?
choices: So everyone can see where every wall, door and window goes
So the plan is pretty on the wall
harder.a: So everyone can see where every wall, door and window goes
harder.why: A plan from above shows the whole layout at once.

harder.q: A plan shows a wardrobe blocking a window. What is the best fix?
choices: Move the wardrobe to a wall with no window
Take the window off the plan
harder.a: Move the wardrobe to a wall with no window
harder.why: Light and a view matter, so the furniture moves, not the window.

harder.q: Two rooms in a plan are very dark. What could an architect change?
choices: Make the windows bigger or add a window facing the sun
harder.a: Make the windows bigger or add a window facing the sun
harder.why: Windows let in daylight, so bigger or better-placed windows help.

harder.q: A builder says a wall in the plan is too thin to hold up the floor above. What should the architect do?
choices: Check the drawing and make the wall thicker or add support
Take the floor out of the plan
harder.a: Check the drawing and make the wall thicker or add support
harder.why: Architects check strength with builders before work starts.

learn.text: Pilots fly planes. Before take-off they check the plane and the weather.
Pilots talk to air traffic control. They help planes stay apart and land safely.

quiz.q: What do pilots check before take-off?

choices: In the cabin with the seats

challenge.scene: The airport is very foggy, and the plane cannot see the runway well.
challenge.question: Ask a pilot: what are some ways the plane could still land safely?
choices: Use the instruments to see the way down
Fly straight at the ground and hope
Wait for the fog to be a different colour

task.prompt: First pass: which of these should a pilot check before take-off?
task.a: The fuel

harder.q: Fog covers the runway. What tool helps a pilot find the way down?
choices: A torch held out of the window
harder.a: The instruments in the cockpit
harder.why: Instruments show height and direction when the view is poor.

harder.q: Why do pilots talk to air traffic control?
choices: To ask about the weather in other countries only
To get permission and stay safely apart from other planes
harder.a: To get permission and stay safely apart from other planes
harder.why: Air traffic control keeps planes apart and guides them.

harder.q: An engine warning light comes on during a flight. What should the pilot do?
choices: Follow the checklist and tell air traffic control
Turn off all the lights and hope
harder.a: Follow the checklist and tell air traffic control
harder.why: Checklists and reporting keep everyone safe.

harder.q: Why do pilots check the fuel before a flight?
choices: To make the plane lighter for fun
To be sure there is enough to reach the destination
harder.a: To be sure there is enough to reach the destination
harder.why: The plane needs enough fuel for the whole journey.

harder.q: The wind is strong at the airport. What helps the plane land?
harder.a: Landing into the wind
harder.why: Landing into the wind slows the plane down and makes landing easier.

learn.text: Artists make pictures to show feelings and ideas.
Artists mix colours. Mixing yellow and blue makes green.

quiz.q: What colour do you get from red and yellow?
What do artists use to paint?

challenge.scene: You only have blue and yellow paint, and you want to paint a tree.
challenge.question: Ask an artist: what could you make, and how?
choices: Mix the blue and yellow to make green

task.prompt: First pass: which mix makes green?
task.a: Blue and yellow

harder.q: A painting looks flat. What could an artist add to make it look deeper?
choices: Darker colours in the back and lighter ones in front
harder.a: Darker colours in the back and lighter ones in front
harder.why: Dark and light shades make things look near or far away.

harder.q: Why do artists look at a real object before painting it?
choices: To see the shapes, shadows and colours clearly
harder.a: To see the shapes, shadows and colours clearly
harder.why: Looking closely helps the picture look real or true to what the artist sees.

harder.q: An artist wants a calm picture. Which colours would help?
harder.a: Soft blues and greens
harder.why: Cool, soft colours feel calm.

harder.q: Why do artists sketch before painting?
choices: To plan the picture and try ideas
harder.a: To plan the picture and try ideas
harder.why: A sketch lets the artist test ideas before the real painting.

harder.q: A painting has too much red in one corner. What could help balance it?
choices: Paint over it all in red
Add a cooler colour or a shape on the other side
harder.a: Add a cooler colour or a shape on the other side
harder.why: Balancing colours and shapes makes a picture feel even.

learn.text: Flight attendants look after everyone on a plane. They say hello and show people their seats.
They show how to buckle a seat belt and where the exits are. They know what to do if something goes wrong.

quiz.q: What do flight attendants show people?
choices: How to buckle a seat belt
quiz.a: How to buckle a seat belt

quiz.q: Who looks after everyone on the plane?
What do they know about the exits?

challenge.scene: A child on the plane is feeling worried about the bumpy ride.
challenge.question: Ask a flight attendant: what are some ways to help them feel calm?
choices: Sit with them and talk about something fun
Tell them to stop being scared
Turn the lights off and leave them alone

task.prompt: First pass: what should a flight attendant do before take-off?
choices: Check that every seat belt is fastened
task.a: Check that every seat belt is fastened

harder.q: A passenger asks how to get out in an emergency. What is the best way to help?
choices: Tell them to look for it themselves
Point to the exits and show the nearest one
Tell them to hide in the toilet
harder.a: Point to the exits and show the nearest one
harder.why: Showing the nearest exit is quick and clear.

harder.q: A drink cart is in the aisle when the plane starts to shake. What should the flight attendant do?
choices: Make the cart safe and sit down with a seat belt on
Hold the cart up while standing
harder.a: Make the cart safe and sit down with a seat belt on
harder.why: Safety first: secure the cart and sit down.

harder.q: A child has lost a toy on the plane. What should the flight attendant do?
choices: Tell the child to find another plane
Help look for it and keep the child calm
Say it is not their problem
harder.a: Help look for it and keep the child calm
harder.why: Helping and calming the child is the kind thing to do.

harder.q: Why does a flight attendant count the people on the plane?
choices: To check everyone is safe and seated before take-off
harder.a: To check everyone is safe and seated before take-off
harder.why: Everyone must be seated and belted before the plane moves.

harder.q: A passenger is sick and feels dizzy. What should the flight attendant do first?
choices: Ask them to stand up and walk
Tell the crew and help them sit or lie down
harder.a: Tell the crew and help them sit or lie down
harder.why: Sitting or lying down and telling the crew keeps them safe.

learn.text: Dancers move to music. They use their arms, legs and whole body to tell a story.
Dancers practise the same moves again and again until they feel easy and strong.

quiz.q: What do dancers use to tell a story?
How do dancers get good at a move?
choices: They practise it again and again
They wait for it to happen
quiz.a: They practise it again and again

challenge.scene: A dance is about a sad day, but the music is very happy.
challenge.question: Ask a dancer: what are some ways to show a sad story with your body?
choices: Move slowly and let your arms droop
Jump as high as you can

task.prompt: First pass: which move would show a happy feeling?
choices: Spinning round with your arms up
task.a: Spinning round with your arms up

harder.q: A dancer forgets a move during a show. What is the best thing to do?
choices: Keep moving to the music and follow the others
Stop and walk off the stage
harder.a: Keep moving to the music and follow the others
harder.why: Keeping the rhythm and following the group keeps the show going.

harder.q: A dance should show a storm. Which move shows that best?
choices: Fast, twirling moves with arms flapping
harder.a: Fast, twirling moves with arms flapping
harder.why: Fast, wild movement suggests wind and rain.

harder.q: How does a dancer warm up before a show?
choices: Stretch the body slowly and move the joints
Sit down and eat a big meal
Run as fast as possible without stretching
harder.a: Stretch the body slowly and move the joints
harder.why: Gentle stretching warms the muscles and helps prevent injury.

harder.q: Two dancers are out of step. What helps them stay together?
choices: Each dance at their own speed
Dance with their eyes closed and no music
Count the beats together and watch each other
harder.a: Count the beats together and watch each other
harder.why: Counting and watching keep the group in time.

harder.q: A dancer feels nervous before going on stage. What might help?
choices: Eat a big meal just before
Take slow deep breaths and remember the first move
harder.a: Take slow deep breaths and remember the first move
harder.why: Slow breathing and a clear start calm nerves.

learn.text: Singers sing songs with their voice. They breathe deep so the song can be heard.
Singers learn the words and the tune. They practise until they can sing them clearly.

quiz.q: What do singers use to make a song?
What helps a singer be heard?

challenge.scene: The audience is far away at the back of a big hall.
challenge.question: Ask a singer: what are some ways to make sure everyone can hear you?
choices: Sing with a strong breath and face the back
Sing with your eyes closed and sit down

task.prompt: First pass: what helps a singer sing a long note?
choices: Holding the breath for no reason
task.a: A big, steady breath

harder.q: A singer's voice goes hoarse before a concert. What should they do?
choices: Sing all night to get used to it
Rest their voice and drink water
harder.a: Rest their voice and drink water
harder.why: Rest and water help the voice recover; straining it makes things worse.

harder.q: What helps a singer stay in tune?
choices: Listening carefully and matching the note
Changing the words as they go
harder.a: Listening carefully and matching the note
harder.why: Listening to the note and matching it keeps the voice in tune.

harder.q: A song is too high to reach. What is a good idea?
choices: Squeeze the voice higher and strain
Sing it in a lower key
Shout the note instead of singing it
harder.a: Sing it in a lower key
harder.why: Singing lower keeps the voice relaxed and healthy.

harder.q: Why do singers warm up with gentle humming?
choices: It makes the voice louder straight away
It wakes up the voice slowly before singing
harder.a: It wakes up the voice slowly before singing
harder.why: Humming warms the voice gently and reduces strain.

harder.q: A crowd can't hear the singer. What should the singer do?
choices: Turn their back to the crowd
Stand closer to the microphone and breathe from the belly
harder.a: Stand closer to the microphone and breathe from the belly
harder.why: Good breath support and a close microphone make the voice carry.

learn.text: Builders put up walls, roofs and floors. They use bricks, wood and strong nails.
Builders check that each wall stands straight, using a long tool with a bubble in it.

quiz.q: What tool shows if a wall is straight?
What do builders use to join wood?

challenge.scene: The wall you are building is leaning a little to one side.
challenge.question: Ask a builder: what are some ways to fix a wall that leans?
choices: Check it with a level and move the bricks back
Paint it so no one can see
Build the next wall on top of it anyway

task.prompt: First pass: what should a builder check before the roof goes on?
choices: That the walls are straight and strong
task.a: That the walls are straight and strong

harder.q: A builder needs to lift a heavy beam. What is the safest way?
choices: Lift it alone with a straight back
Use a crane or ask others to help and bend the knees
harder.a: Use a crane or ask others to help and bend the knees
harder.why: Lifting with help and proper tools protects everyone.

harder.q: Why do builders wear a hard hat?
choices: To protect the head from falling things
harder.a: To protect the head from falling things
harder.why: Hard hats protect against things that fall on a site.

harder.q: A floor has a sag in the middle. What could fix it?
choices: Add a support beam under the middle
harder.a: Add a support beam under the middle
harder.why: A support beam stops the middle sinking.

harder.q: Which tool checks that a shelf is flat?
harder.a: A spirit level
harder.why: A spirit level shows if a surface is level.

harder.q: Before digging a hole, what should the builder check first?
choices: Where the pipes and cables are underground
harder.a: Where the pipes and cables are underground
harder.why: Hitting a pipe or cable can be dangerous, so the builder checks first.

learn.text: Doctors check people who are sick. They listen to the heart and look in the ears.
Doctors decide how to help people get better. Sometimes that means rest, and sometimes medicine.

quiz.q: What does a doctor listen to?
What does a doctor do when someone is sick?
choices: Checks them to help them get better
quiz.a: Checks them to help them get better

quiz.q: What can help a person get better?

challenge.scene: A friend has a tummy ache and does not want to eat.
challenge.question: Ask a doctor: what are some ways to help a friend feel better?
choices: Let them rest and tell a grown-up
Say it is nothing and ignore them

task.prompt: First pass: what does a doctor use to listen to a heartbeat?
task.a: A stethoscope

harder.q: A patient has a fever and a sore throat. What should a doctor do first?
choices: Send them home without a check
Check the temperature and look at the throat and chest
harder.a: Check the temperature and look at the throat and chest
harder.why: A check shows what is going on before any treatment.

harder.q: Why does a doctor ask questions about how you feel?
choices: To understand what is wrong and how to help
harder.a: To understand what is wrong and how to help
harder.why: Your answers help the doctor find the right help.

harder.q: A child needs medicine. What is most important?
choices: Give it to whoever is closest
Give the right amount at the right time
harder.a: Give the right amount at the right time
harder.why: The right dose at the right time keeps the child safe.

harder.q: Why does a doctor wash their hands before a check?
choices: To make the hands smell nice
harder.a: To stop germs spreading
harder.why: Clean hands stop germs moving from one person to another.

harder.q: A patient is very worried about a check. What helps most?
choices: Explain what will happen and answer their questions
Do the check quickly without speaking
harder.a: Explain what will happen and answer their questions
harder.why: Explaining makes a scary check feel safer.

learn.text: Nurses look after patients in hospital. They check their temperature and give them their medicine.
Nurses help doctors. They keep the beds clean and make sure patients are comfortable.

quiz.q: Where do nurses look after patients?

challenge.scene: A patient is scared of the needle.
challenge.question: Ask a nurse: what are some ways to help the patient feel brave?
choices: Explain each step and hold their hand
Do it quickly without a word
Tell them to look away and not ask

task.prompt: First pass: what should a nurse do before giving medicine?
choices: Check the name and the dose
Give it to the nearest person
task.a: Check the name and the dose

harder.q: A patient's temperature is higher than normal. What should the nurse do?
choices: Write it down and tell the doctor
harder.a: Write it down and tell the doctor
harder.why: A high temperature needs to be recorded and reported.

harder.q: What is the most important thing before giving medicine?
choices: Check the patient's name and the medicine label
harder.a: Check the patient's name and the medicine label
harder.why: Checking the name and label stops the wrong medicine going to the wrong person.

harder.q: A patient asks for a drink, but the doctor has not said they can have one. What should the nurse do?
choices: Explain why and offer a damp cloth for the lips, if the doctor agrees
Give them a big glass anyway
harder.a: Explain why and offer a damp cloth for the lips, if the doctor agrees
harder.why: Some patients must wait, and the nurse explains kindly and checks first.

harder.q: Why do nurses change bandages?
choices: To keep the wound clean and help it heal
harder.a: To keep the wound clean and help it heal
harder.why: Clean dressings stop infection and help healing.

harder.q: A patient is lonely at night. What can the nurse do?
choices: Turn off the lights and leave
Sit with them for a moment and talk kindly
harder.a: Sit with them for a moment and talk kindly
harder.why: Kind company helps patients feel safe.

learn.text: Vets help sick and hurt animals. They check dogs, cats, birds and even hamsters.
Vets are gentle. They talk softly and check each animal carefully before they give any medicine.

quiz.q: What do vets check before medicine?

challenge.scene: A puppy has hurt its paw and keeps trying to run away.
challenge.question: Ask a vet: what are some ways to help the puppy stay calm?
choices: Speak softly and hold the puppy gently
Chase the puppy around the room
Put the puppy in a box and shout

task.prompt: First pass: how should a vet hold a hurt bird?
task.a: Gently, with both hands

harder.q: A dog eats chocolate. What should the vet tell the owner?
choices: Call the vet straight away, chocolate can make dogs very ill
Wait and see for a week
harder.a: Call the vet straight away, chocolate can make dogs very ill
harder.why: Chocolate is toxic to dogs, so a quick call to the vet is vital.

harder.q: A cat won't eat for two days. What is the best next step?
choices: Take it to the vet for a check
Give it lots of fish and wait a month
Put it outside to see what happens
harder.a: Take it to the vet for a check
harder.why: A cat that stops eating needs a check to find out why.

harder.q: Why do vets check an animal's weight?
choices: To see if it is healthy and eating enough
harder.a: To see if it is healthy and eating enough
harder.why: Weight shows whether the animal is growing well or losing weight.

harder.q: A rabbit's teeth are growing too long. What helps?
choices: A vet trims them, and the rabbit gets hay to chew
Give it hard sweets to chew
harder.a: A vet trims them, and the rabbit gets hay to chew
harder.why: Hay helps wear the teeth down, and a vet can trim them safely.

harder.q: How should a vet talk to a scared animal?
choices: They should not talk at all
harder.a: Softly and slowly
harder.why: A calm voice helps an animal trust the person.

learn.text: Teachers help children learn to read, count and write. They make lessons fun.
Teachers help children make friends and feel safe. They listen when someone is worried.

quiz.q: What do teachers help children learn?
What do teachers do when a child is worried?

challenge.scene: A child in the class finds counting very hard and feels sad.
challenge.question: Ask a teacher: what are some ways to help them feel better about counting?
choices: Use counters or toys and praise each step
Tell them they are no good at it
Give them harder sums straight away

task.prompt: First pass: a child has 2 apples and gets 3 more. How many apples now?

harder.q: A child is shy and does not want to read aloud. What helps?
choices: Let them practise first or read to a friend
Make them read to the whole class at once
harder.a: Let them practise first or read to a friend
harder.why: Practice and a safe audience build confidence step by step.

harder.q: Why do teachers use praise?
choices: It makes children want to keep trying
harder.a: It makes children want to keep trying
harder.why: Praise for effort encourages children to keep going.

harder.q: Two children keep arguing at play time. What should a teacher do?
choices: Help them say how each feels and agree on a fix
Tell them the argument does not matter
harder.a: Help them say how each feels and agree on a fix
harder.why: Talking it through teaches children to solve problems together.

harder.q: A child gets a sum wrong. What is the best next step?
choices: Tell them they are bad at maths
Give them the answer and move on
Look at what they did and show them the next step
harder.a: Look at what they did and show them the next step
harder.why: Seeing where the mistake is helps the child learn it.

harder.q: Why do teachers plan a lesson before the day?
choices: So the lesson moves steadily and each child can join in
harder.a: So the lesson moves steadily and each child can join in
harder.why: A plan keeps lessons clear and gives every child a chance to learn.

learn.text: Firefighters put out fires and help people in emergencies. They ride in a big red fire engine.
Firefighters wear special clothes and helmets. They use hoses full of water to put out the fire.

quiz.q: What do firefighters use to put out a fire?

challenge.scene: There is smoke in a house, and a child is in an upstairs room.
challenge.question: Ask a firefighter: what are some ways to get the child out safely?
choices: Crawl low under the smoke and call out to the child
Run up the stairs through thick smoke
Wait until the smoke goes away

task.prompt: First pass: what should you do first if you smell smoke at home?
choices: Tell a grown-up and get out
Go and look for the fire
task.a: Tell a grown-up and get out

harder.q: A fire has started in a kitchen. What should people do first?
choices: Get out and call the fire service
harder.a: Get out and call the fire service
harder.why: Leaving quickly and calling for help keeps everyone safe.

harder.q: Why should you never use a lift in a fire?
choices: It can stop working or take you to the fire
harder.a: It can stop working or take you to the fire
harder.why: A lift can fail in a fire, so the stairs are safer.

harder.q: How should you move through smoke?
choices: Low to the floor, where the air is cleaner
harder.a: Low to the floor, where the air is cleaner
harder.why: Smoke rises, so the air is clearest near the floor.

harder.q: A firefighter sees a car that might catch fire. What should they do?
choices: Keep people away and call for more help
Walk up to it to see
harder.a: Keep people away and call for more help
harder.why: Keeping people back and calling for help keeps everyone safer.

harder.q: Why do firefighters practise drills?
choices: So everyone knows what to do quickly in a real emergency
So the fire engine gets dirty
harder.a: So everyone knows what to do quickly in a real emergency
harder.why: Drills make the right actions automatic when it matters.

learn.text: Police officers keep people safe. They help find lost things and lost people.
Police officers listen to everyone and help them. They tell the truth and treat people fairly.

quiz.q: What do police officers help people do?
How do police officers treat people?

challenge.scene: A child has got separated from their family in a busy shop.
challenge.question: Ask a police officer: what are some ways to help the child find their family?
choices: Take the child to a safe place and ask for their name
Leave the child on their own

task.prompt: First pass: what should a lost child do?
choices: Stay where they are and find a grown-up in uniform
Walk off to find home alone
task.a: Stay where they are and find a grown-up in uniform

harder.q: Someone finds a wallet on the street. What should they do?
choices: Hand it to a police station or a grown-up
harder.a: Hand it to a police station or a grown-up
harder.why: Handing it in lets the owner get it back.

harder.q: A child on a bike is not wearing a helmet near a busy road. What might a police officer do?
choices: Shout at them in front of everyone
Talk to them kindly about safety
harder.a: Talk to them kindly about safety
harder.why: Kind advice helps a child remember to stay safe.

harder.q: Why do police officers listen to both sides in a problem?
choices: So they understand what happened fairly
So they can decide on lunch
harder.a: So they understand what happened fairly
harder.why: Hearing both sides helps find the truth.

harder.q: A road is blocked by a fallen tree. What should a police officer do?
choices: Drive around it on the pavement
Set up a warning and tell other drivers a different way
harder.a: Set up a warning and tell other drivers a different way
harder.why: Warnings and a diversion keep drivers and people safe.

harder.q: A phone call says someone is hurt. What is the right thing to do?
choices: Wait and see if they feel better
Call the emergency number and say where it is and what happened
harder.a: Call the emergency number and say where it is and what happened
harder.why: Quick, clear information gets help to the right place.

learn.text: Chefs cook meals in a restaurant. They chop, stir and taste to make the food right.
Chefs make new recipes. They try different mixes of food and keep the ones that taste best.

quiz.q: What do chefs do to check food?

challenge.scene: A soup is too salty, and the customers are waiting.
challenge.question: Ask a chef: what are some ways to fix the soup?
choices: Add water or potato to soak up some salt
Serve it anyway without a word
Add more salt to hide it

task.prompt: First pass: what should a chef do before cooking?
task.a: Wash their hands

harder.q: A cake is too dry. What should the chef check first?
choices: The amount of liquid or butter and the baking time
How long it was in the freezer
harder.a: The amount of liquid or butter and the baking time
harder.why: Too little liquid or too long in the oven makes cake dry.

harder.q: Why do chefs keep raw meat away from salad?
choices: To stop germs spreading to food that is not cooked
To make the salad look red
harder.a: To stop germs spreading to food that is not cooked
harder.why: Raw meat can carry germs that spread to other food.

harder.q: A new recipe tastes flat. What might help?
choices: A squeeze of lemon or a pinch of salt
harder.a: A squeeze of lemon or a pinch of salt
harder.why: Lemon and salt wake up flavours.

harder.q: Why does a chef taste food while cooking?
choices: To check the flavour and adjust it
harder.a: To check the flavour and adjust it
harder.why: Tasting lets the chef adjust salt, sweetness or sourness.

harder.q: Two dishes need to be ready at the same time. What should the chef do?
choices: Cook both in the same pan
Plan the order and use a timer for each dish
harder.a: Plan the order and use a timer for each dish
harder.why: A plan and timers make sure both dishes are ready hot.

learn.text: Bakers make bread, cakes and biscuits. They get up early so the bread is warm for breakfast.
Bakers mix flour, water and yeast to make bread dough. The dough rises before it goes in the oven.

challenge.scene: The bread dough is not rising, and the shop opens soon.
challenge.question: Ask a baker: what are some ways to fix it?
choices: Check the yeast and put the dough somewhere warm
Bake it flat and hope for the best

task.prompt: First pass: which of these goes into bread dough?
task.a: Flour

harder.q: The bread is too hard and dry. What could be the reason?
choices: It was baked in the morning
It was in the oven too long or the dough had too little water
harder.a: It was in the oven too long or the dough had too little water
harder.why: Too long in the oven or too little water dries bread out.

harder.q: Why does dough need to rest?
choices: So the flour soaks up water and it is easier to shape
harder.a: So the flour soaks up water and it is easier to shape

choices: A slow voice and droopy shoulders
task.a: A slow voice and droopy shoulders

harder.q: An actor forgets their line on stage. What is the best thing to do?
choices: Improvise a line that fits and keep the scene going
Wait in silence until the curtain falls
harder.a: Improvise a line that fits and keep the scene going
harder.why: Keeping the scene going is what the audience needs.

harder.q: Why do actors warm up their voices before a play?
choices: To make the voice clear and strong for the audience
harder.a: To make the voice clear and strong for the audience
harder.why: A warm voice carries and sounds clear.

harder.q: An actor must play a very quiet, sad character. How can they show it?
choices: Speak softly with a slow pace and low energy
harder.a: Speak softly with a slow pace and low energy
harder.why: Quiet voice and slow movement show sadness.

harder.q: Why do actors practise with the other actors?
choices: So they can pick their costumes
So they know how to respond and move together
harder.a: So they know how to respond and move together
harder.why: Practising together makes the scene feel real.

harder.q: An actor is nervous before going on stage. What helps?
choices: Breathe slowly and focus on the first line

learn.text: Engineers design and fix machines, bridges and gadgets. They work out how things fit and move.
Engineers test their designs. If something breaks, they find out why and make it stronger.

quiz.q: What do engineers do with a design?
What do engineers do if something breaks?
choices: Find out why and make it stronger
quiz.a: Find out why and make it stronger

challenge.scene: A bridge made of sticks keeps bending in the middle.
challenge.question: Ask an engineer: what are some ways to make the bridge stronger?
choices: Add triangle supports across the middle

task.prompt: First pass: what shape is strongest for holding weight in a bridge?
task.a: A triangle

harder.q: A bridge design must hold a heavy bus. What should an engineer do?
choices: Guess how heavy a bus is
Calculate the weight and test the design with models
harder.a: Calculate the weight and test the design with models
harder.why: Calculation and testing show the bridge will be strong enough.

harder.q: Why do engineers test machines in a safe space first?
choices: To find problems before anyone uses them
So it gets a new colour
harder.a: To find problems before anyone uses them
harder.why: Testing first finds problems safely.

harder.q: A gear is slipping. What might be the cause?
choices: The teeth are worn or the gear is not lined up
The gear is too heavy to move
harder.a: The teeth are worn or the gear is not lined up
harder.why: Worn teeth or misalignment make gears slip.

harder.q: Why do engineers use a lever?
choices: To lift something heavy with less effort
harder.a: To lift something heavy with less effort
harder.why: A lever multiplies the force you put in.

harder.q: A tower leans in the wind. What should an engineer add?
choices: Supports or a wider base to keep it steady
harder.a: Supports or a wider base to keep it steady
harder.why: A wider base and supports stop a tower tipping.

learn.text: Coders write instructions for computers. These instructions make apps and games work.
Coders test their code. When it does not work, they find the bug and fix it.

quiz.q: What do coders do with their code?

challenge.scene: A game character walks through walls when it should stop at them.
challenge.question: Ask a coder: what are some ways to find and fix this?
choices: Check the wall rule and test it step by step
Remove all the walls from the game
Tell the player it is a feature

task.prompt: First pass: what should a coder do when a game does not work?
choices: Find the mistake and test it again
Turn off the computer and forget it
task.a: Find the mistake and test it again

harder.q: A program crashes when a user types their name with a space. What should a coder do?
choices: Test with spaces and find where the code breaks
Tell the user not to use spaces
harder.a: Test with spaces and find where the code breaks
harder.why: Testing the case shows the bug, and then it can be fixed.

harder.q: Why do coders break a big problem into smaller steps?
choices: So each step is easy to test and fix
harder.a: So each step is easy to test and fix
harder.why: Small steps are easier to test and fix.

harder.q: What is a loop in code?
choices: Something that repeats the same instructions
harder.a: Something that repeats the same instructions
harder.why: A loop repeats instructions a set number of times or until something happens.

harder.q: Why do coders write notes in their code?
choices: So other people can understand what the code does
So the computer can read them faster
harder.a: So other people can understand what the code does
harder.why: Notes help other people, and future you, understand the code.

harder.q: A button in an app does nothing when pressed. What is a good first check?
choices: Look at what the button is set to do and test it
Restart the phone and forget it
harder.a: Look at what the button is set to do and test it
harder.why: Checking what the button is set to do finds the mistake.

learn.text: Electricians put in and fix the wires that bring power to buildings. Power makes lights and fridges work.
Electricians always switch off the power before they touch a wire. Safety comes first.

quiz.q: What do electricians do before touching a wire?

challenge.scene: A lamp in the house keeps flickering, and it is getting dark.
challenge.question: Ask an electrician: what are some ways to find out why?
choices: Check the bulb and get an electrician to look at the wiring
Put your fingers in the socket to see
Ignore it and keep the lamp on

task.prompt: First pass: what should you do before you change a light bulb?
choices: Switch the lamp off and let it cool
Put a fork in the socket
task.a: Switch the lamp off and let it cool

harder.q: A socket feels warm. What should an electrician do?
choices: Turn off the power and check the wires and plug
harder.a: Turn off the power and check the wires and plug
harder.why: A warm socket can mean a loose or faulty connection, so turn the power off and check.

harder.q: Why do electricians use coloured wires?
choices: Because the colour makes the power faster
To tell which wire does what and make it safe
harder.a: To tell which wire does what and make it safe
harder.why: Colours show each wire's job so it is connected correctly.

harder.q: A fuse keeps blowing. What does it mean?
choices: The fuse wants to be bigger
There may be too much power or a fault in the circuit
harder.a: There may be too much power or a fault in the circuit
harder.why: A blown fuse is a warning that something is overloaded or faulty.

harder.q: Why do electricians wear rubber gloves?
choices: To stop electricity passing through the body
harder.a: To stop electricity passing through the body
harder.why: Rubber does not conduct electricity, so it protects the hands.

harder.q: A light switch feels hot. What should be done?
choices: Turn off the power and get an electrician to check it
Turn it on and off quickly
Touch it to see if it is still hot
harder.a: Turn off the power and get an electrician to check it
harder.why: A hot switch can be dangerous, so the power needs to go off and a professional should check it.

learn.text: Hairdressers cut, wash and style hair. They ask how the person wants their hair to look.
Hairdressers are careful with scissors. They cut a little at a time, so the hair looks just right.

choices: How the person wants their hair
quiz.a: How the person wants their hair

challenge.scene: A customer wants a short haircut, but they are worried it will look silly.
challenge.question: Ask a hairdresser: what are some ways to help them feel happy with it?
choices: Show them a picture and cut a little at a time
Cut it very short straight away
Tell them it is too late to change

task.prompt: First pass: what should a hairdresser do before they start cutting?
choices: Ask what style the customer wants
task.a: Ask what style the customer wants

harder.q: A customer's hair is very dry and frizzy. What might help?
choices: A gentle conditioner and less heat from the dryer
Hot water and a lot of scrubbing
harder.a: A gentle conditioner and less heat from the dryer
harder.why: Gentle care and less heat help dry hair.

harder.q: Why do hairdressers ask about allergies before colouring?
choices: Some hair dyes can irritate the skin
harder.a: Some hair dyes can irritate the skin
harder.why: Some dyes can cause a reaction, so checking first keeps the customer safe.

harder.q: A child is nervous about a haircut. What helps?
choices: Explain each step and let them hold a mirror
Cut quickly so they don't see
harder.a: Explain each step and let them hold a mirror
harder.why: Explaining and letting them see helps them feel safe.

harder.q: Why do hairdressers check the hair is dry before cutting?
choices: Dry hair is faster to sweep up
Wet hair is too heavy to cut
Wet hair stretches, so the cut might end up shorter than planned
harder.a: Wet hair stretches, so the cut might end up shorter than planned
harder.why: Hair stretches when wet, so a cut on wet hair can be too short.

harder.q: What does a hairdresser use to thin out hair?
harder.a: Thinning scissors
harder.why: Thinning scissors remove some hair without making it all short.

learn.text: Florists make bunches of flowers for people to give to friends, family and at special events.
Florists pick flowers that go well together. They trim the stems so the flowers can drink water.

quiz.q: Why do florists trim the stems?
choices: So the flowers can drink water
quiz.a: So the flowers can drink water

quiz.q: What do florists think about when they choose flowers?
choices: Which ones are on the ground

challenge.scene: A customer wants flowers for a friend who likes only one colour.
challenge.question: Ask a florist: what are some ways to make a bunch just for them?
choices: Use a mix of their favourite colour with some green leaves
Make the bunch without any flowers

task.prompt: First pass: what should a florist do with the stems before putting them in water?
task.a: Trim them at a slant

harder.q: A bunch of flowers wilts after one day. What is a likely reason?
choices: The stems are not in water or have not been trimmed
harder.a: The stems are not in water or have not been trimmed
harder.why: Stems need water and a fresh trim to drink well.

harder.q: Why does a florist use a mix of sizes?
choices: To make the bunch look full and balanced
To make it heavier to carry
harder.a: To make the bunch look full and balanced
harder.why: Mixed sizes give a balanced, full shape.

harder.q: A customer wants flowers that last a long time. What should the florist pick?
choices: Long-lasting flowers like carnations or chrysanthemums
Flowers that have already started to brown at the edges
Petals that fall off in a breeze
harder.a: Long-lasting flowers like carnations or chrysanthemums
harder.why: Carnations and chrysanthemums last longer in a vase.

harder.q: Why does a florist add a little water to a bunch before handing it over?
choices: To keep the flowers fresh on the way home
harder.a: To keep the flowers fresh on the way home
harder.why: Water keeps the stems fresh until they are in a vase.

harder.q: What is a good colour mix for a birthday bunch?
choices: Bright colours that the person likes
harder.a: Bright colours that the person likes
harder.why: Choosing favourite colours makes the gift special.

learn.text: Tailors sew and mend clothes, so they fit well. They measure the person first.
Tailors take in or let out seams, so a jumper or a skirt fits just right.

choices: Cut the cloth in half and stop

quiz.q: What do tailors change so clothes fit?

challenge.scene: A child's new coat is too big in the arms.
challenge.question: Ask a tailor: what are some ways to make the coat fit better?
choices: Take in the sleeves and check the fit again
Let the arms out even more
Tell the child to grow into it straight away

task.prompt: First pass: what should a tailor do before cutting the cloth?
task.a: Measure carefully

harder.q: A dress has a split at the seam. What should the tailor do?
choices: Mend the seam with strong stitches and check the fit
harder.a: Mend the seam with strong stitches and check the fit
harder.why: Strong stitching repairs the seam properly.

harder.q: Why do tailors pin fabric before sewing?
choices: To hold the pieces in the right place
harder.a: To hold the pieces in the right place
harder.why: Pins keep the fabric lined up while sewing.

harder.q: A shirt sleeve is too long. What should be done?
choices: Measure, mark the new length and shorten it neatly
Leave it and roll it up
harder.a: Measure, mark the new length and shorten it neatly
harder.why: Measuring and marking gives a neat, even hem.

harder.q: Why do tailors keep a tape measure round their neck?
choices: It is handy for measuring quickly
harder.a: It is handy for measuring quickly
harder.why: A tape to hand saves time when measuring.

harder.q: What should a tailor check when a jacket fits strangely?
choices: The colour of the buttons only

learn.text: Beekeepers look after bees and collect their honey. They keep the bee homes, called hives, tidy and dry.
Beekeepers wear a special suit and a veil, to stay safe. They move slowly, so the bees stay calm.

quiz.q: What do beekeepers wear to stay safe?
choices: A special suit and a veil
quiz.a: A special suit and a veil

challenge.scene: A bee is buzzing close to a child in the garden.
challenge.question: Ask a beekeeper: what are some ways to keep everyone safe and the bee calm?
choices: Stay still and let the bee fly away on its own

task.prompt: First pass: what should a beekeeper do before opening a hive?
choices: Put on the suit and veil
task.a: Put on the suit and veil

harder.q: A hive is too hot in the summer. What can the beekeeper do?
choices: Give the hive shade and make sure air and water are close by
harder.a: Give the hive shade and make sure air and water are close by
harder.why: Shade, airflow and water help the bees keep cool.

harder.q: Why do beekeepers check for disease in the hive?
choices: To keep the bees healthy and protect the hive
harder.a: To keep the bees healthy and protect the hive
harder.why: Checking early helps stop disease spreading.

harder.q: What is a swarm?
choices: A large group of bees moving to start a new hive
harder.a: A large group of bees moving to start a new hive
harder.why: A swarm is bees leaving to make a new home.

harder.q: A beekeeper wants to take honey. What should they leave in the hive?
choices: All of it, the bees have plenty
Enough honey for the bees to eat through the winter
harder.a: Enough honey for the bees to eat through the winter
harder.why: Bees need honey to survive the cold months.

harder.q: Why do beekeepers use smoke?
choices: It calms the bees so they are easier to work with
It keeps the flies away from the lunch
harder.a: It calms the bees so they are easier to work with
harder.why: Smoke calms bees so the beekeeper can work safely.
